- Before all 8 platforms are active, only the available platforms are ranked (ranks may not fill 1–8 completely).
- Spotify is included as a streaming subscription platform (audio) alongside video services for a holistic view of the subscription landscape.

- **unit**: Ordinal rank (1–8); lower values = higher subscriber count.

## Data Notes
- Rankings are estimated based on publicly reported subscriber figures and industry analyst estimates; exact subscriber counts are not provided.
- Disney+ launched November 2019 (first appears Q4 2019). Apple TV+ launched November 2019 (first appears Q4 2019). HBO Max launched May 2020 (first appears Q2 2020).
- Before all 8 platforms are active, only the available platforms are ranked (ranks may not fill 1–8 completely).
- Spotify is included as a streaming subscription platform (audio) alongside video services for a holistic view of the subscription landscape.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
import json

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    source = json.load(f)

data = source['streaming_rankings']['data']
platforms = source['streaming_rankings']['platforms']

# Build quarter labels and rank arrays
quarters = [d['quarter'] for d in data]
x_indices = list(range(len(quarters)))

ranks = {}
for p in platforms:
    ranks[p] = [d[p] for d in data]

# Color palette — business/editorial, distinct and accessible
colors = {
    'Netflix':           '#E50914',   # Netflix red
    'Amazon Prime Video':'#00A8E1',   # Prime blue
    'Spotify':           '#1DB954',   # Spotify green
    'Disney+':           '#113CCF',   # Disney+ deep blue
    'Apple TV+':         '#A2AAAD',   # Apple gray
    'HBO Max':           '#B01EFF',   # HBO purple
    'YouTube Premium':   '#FF0000',   # YouTube red — will be adjusted for contrast
    'Hulu':              '#1CE783',   # Hulu green — will be adjusted
}

# Adjust YouTube and Hulu colors for better contrast against Netflix/Spotify
colors['YouTube Premium'] = '#FF6B35'  # Orange instead of red (avoids Netflix clash)
colors['Hulu'] = '#7CB342'             # Olive green (avoids Spotify clash)

# Line widths — emphasize key narratives
def get_lw(platform):
    if platform == 'Netflix':
        return 4.0
    if platform == 'Disney+':
        return 3.5
    if platform in ('Amazon Prime Video', 'Spotify'):
        return 2.5
    return 1.8

def get_alpha(platform):
    if platform in ('Netflix', 'Disney+'):
        return 1.0
    if platform in ('Amazon Prime Video', 'Spotify'):
        return 0.9
    return 0.7

# Set up figure
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(20, 9))
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')
ax.set_facecolor('#FAFAFA')

# Invert y-axis: rank 1 at top
ax.set_ylim(8.6, 0.4)

# Plot lines
for platform in platforms:
    y_vals = ranks[platform]
    x_vals = []
    y_plot = []
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(x_indices, y_vals)):
        if y is not None:
            x_vals.append(x)
            y_plot.append(y)

    if len(x_vals) < 2:
        continue

    ax.plot(x_vals, y_plot,
            color=colors[platform],
            linewidth=get_lw(platform),
            alpha=get_alpha(platform),
            solid_capstyle='round',
            zorder=3 if platform in ('Netflix', 'Disney+') else 2)

    # Start label
    start_idx = 0
    start_y = y_plot[start_idx]
    start_x = x_vals[start_idx]
    ax.annotate(platform,
                xy=(start_x - 0.15, start_y),
                xytext=(-12, 0),
                textcoords='offset points',
                ha='right', va='center',
                fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold',
                color=colors[platform])

    # End label
    end_idx = len(x_vals) - 1
    end_y = y_plot[end_idx]
    end_x = x_vals[end_idx]
    ax.annotate(platform,
                xy=(end_x + 0.15, end_y),
                xytext=(12, 0),
                textcoords='offset points',
                ha='left', va='center',
                fontsize=9.5, fontweight='bold',
                color=colors[platform])

# Dots at each data point
for platform in platforms:
    y_vals = ranks[platform]
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(x_indices, y_vals)):
        if y is not None:
            size = 7 if platform in ('Netflix', 'Disney+') else 4.5
            ax.plot(x, y, 'o', color=colors[platform],
                    markersize=size, zorder=5 if platform in ('Netflix', 'Disney+') else 4,
                    alpha=get_alpha(platform))

# Highlight Disney+ ascent with a shaded region
disney_x = []
disney_y = []
for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(x_indices, ranks['Disney+'])):
    if y is not None:
        disney_x.append(x)
        disney_y.append(y)

if len(disney_x) >= 2:
    # Add a subtle annotation arrow for Disney+'s rise
    ax.annotate("Disney+ rises\nfrom #6 → #3\nin 5 quarters",
                xy=(x_indices[7], 3),  # Q4 2020, rank 3
                xytext=(x_indices[7] + 2.5, 2.0),
                fontsize=9, fontstyle='italic', color=colors['Disney+'],
                ha='center', va='bottom',
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=colors['Disney+'],
                                lw=1.5, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=-0.2'),
                bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white',
                          edgecolor=colors['Disney+'], alpha=0.9))

# Netflix sustained lead annotation
ax.annotate("Netflix holds #1\nfor 25 consecutive quarters",
            xy=(x_indices[12], 1),  # Q1 2022
            xytext=(x_indices[12], 1.65),
            fontsize=9, fontstyle='italic', color=colors['Netflix'],
            ha='center', va='bottom',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='white',
                      edgecolor=colors['Netflix'], alpha=0.9))

# Mid-tier jostling annotation — bracket the 5-8 zone
mid_x_start = x_indices[10]  # Q3 2021
mid_x_end = x_indices[22]    # Q3 2024
ax.annotate("Competitive volatility:\nrank 5–8 zone",
            xy=((mid_x_start + mid_x_end) / 2, 6.5),
            fontsize=8.5, fontstyle='italic', color='#555555',
            ha='center', va='center',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#F0F0F0',
                      edgecolor='#AAAAAA', alpha=0.9))

# Stable top-4 annotation
ax.annotate("Stable top 4",
            xy=(x_indices[18], 3.5),
            fontsize=8.5, fontstyle='italic', color='#555555',
            ha='center', va='center',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', facecolor='#F0F0F0',
                      edgecolor='#AAAAAA', alpha=0.9))

# X-axis formatting
ax.set_xticks(x_indices)
# Show every other quarter label to avoid clutter, but show all tick marks
labels = []
for i, q in enumerate(quarters):
    if i % 2 == 0 or i == len(quarters) - 1:
        labels.append(q)
    else:
        labels.append('')
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=9)

# Y-axis formatting
ax.set_yticks(range(1, 9))
ax.set_yticklabels([f'#{i}' for i in range(1, 9)], fontsize=10, fontweight='medium')

# Grid
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='-', alpha=0.3, color='#CCCCCC')
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.15, color='#CCCCCC')

# Remove top/right spines
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
for spine in ['bottom', 'left']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_color('#CCCCCC')

# Title
ax.set_title('Streaming Platform Subscriber Rankings (Q1 2019 – Q1 2025)',
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20, color='#222222')

# Subtitle
ax.text(0.5, 1.02, 'Quarterly rank position based on global subscriber counts  |  Rank 1 = highest subscribers',
        transform=ax.transAxes, ha='center', va='bottom',
        fontsize=10, color='#666666', fontstyle='italic')

# Axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Quarter', fontsize=11, labelpad=10, color='#444444')
ax.set_ylabel('Rank Position', fontsize=11, labelpad=10, color='#444444')

# Source note
fig.text(0.99, 0.01, 'Source: Estimated from publicly reported subscriber figures & industry analyst estimates',
         ha='right', va='bottom', fontsize=7.5, color='#999999', fontstyle='italic')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.90, bottom=0.15)

plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=200, bbox_inches='tight',
            facecolor=fig.get_facecolor(), edgecolor='none')
plt.close()
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
